stem: Electron affinity of noble gases is (a) very high (b) low (c) almost approaching zero (d) high

key: c O⁻ ion will tend to resist the addition of another electron
stem: The formation of the oxide ion O²⁻(g) requires first an exothermic and then an endothermic step: O(g)+e⁻→O⁻(g), ΔH = −142 kJ mol⁻¹; O⁻(g)+e⁻→O²⁻(g), ΔH = +748 kJ mol⁻¹. This is because (a) O⁻ ion has comparatively larger size than the oxygen atom (b) oxygen has higher electron affinity (c) O⁻ ion will tend to resist the addition of another electron (d) oxygen is more electronegative

key: b ΔH₁ is negative but ΔH₂ is positive due to electron–electron repulsion
stem: Consider O(g) → O⁻(g) (ΔH₁) and O⁻(g) → O²⁻(g) (ΔH₂). Which statement is correct? (a) ΔH₁ and ΔH₂ are both negative (b) ΔH₁ is negative but ΔH₂ is positive due to electron–electron repulsion (c) ΔH₂ is negative because oxide ion is more stable (d) ΔH₂ is smaller in magnitude than ΔH₁
